chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Talib, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A man from the Ansar asked him, 'To whom shall I be righteous?' He said, 'Your parents.' He said, 'They have passed away.' He said, 'Be righteous with your children.'

key_terms.أَبَرُّ: more righteous / to be more righteous to

ai.seo_question: Who should I be righteous to after my parents have passed away?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the dynamic nature of *birr* (righteousness) by establishing a sequential hierarchy: after parents, the primary duty shifts to one's children. This highlights the Shia emphasis on active familial stewardship, where the responsibility of righteousness is not static but adapts to the presence and needs of the next generation, ensuring the continuity of moral and spiritual care within the family unit.
